_comment: The measured truth about the physical rig. Everything reads this. All values null until they are measured. Bump version and re-measure whenever the rig physically changes: different platform, different guitar, exciter moved, amp gain touched, interface settings changed. Version 0 means nothing has been measured yet.
_platform_note: Bela Gem Stereo (Starter Kit, PocketBeagle 2 base; Bela store order #502852), on hand since 2026-09-10. See docs/ground-rules-and-facts.md 3.1 and docs/phase-plan.md. Earlier measurements on a different rig are tagged to their own profile version in logs/README.md, not carried into this file.
_v3_note: Bumped from v2 2026-09-13 (CLAUDE.md rule 13): the M4 buffer/preamp was removed from the signal chain after being confirmed as the source of a ground loop (shared USB ground with the Mac tethering Bela -- see ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.4). All v2 gain_staging measurements involving the M4 are retired below, not carried forward as current. The guitar now runs direct/unbuffered into Bela's audio in; a passive DI box is on order to restore buffering without reintroducing the ground loop.
_signal_chain_note: As actually wired 2026-09-13: Epiphone (humbucker) -> Bela Gem audio in DIRECTLY, unbuffered (temporary -- M4 removed, DI box on order); Bela Gem audio out -> power amp (Dayton DTA120) -> exciter (Dayton), straight through, no pedal or other device in between. Guitar is mono, Bela audio in is stereo -- expect signal on channel 0 (left) only, unconfirmed by measurement yet. See ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.5 for the fail-safe decision this relies on: no hardware kill switch, because there is no separate uncontrolled acoustic loop in this build and the DTA120+exciter's worst case is judged safe by Abel.
_spec_disclaimer: Every value in 'host', 'loop' etc. below is null. The Bela Gem Stereo numbers that are known from the published spec (2 in / 2 out, up to 24-bit / 96 kHz, 8 analog in, no analog out, PocketBeagle 2, USB-C) are recorded as _spec_* notes, NOT as measurements. Phase 0/1 fills in the real values.

host._spec_base_board_note: Multi-core. Migration guide asks for safer inter-thread patterns.
host._spec_sample_rate_note: Gem Stereo supports up to 24-bit / 96 kHz. 44100 is the board's DEFAULT project setting, observed 2026-09-11 running bela/io-check-input/ with no rate specified -- not yet the deliberate Phase 0/1 choice (44.1 / 48 / 96 still open).
host._block_size_note: Board default, same caveat as sample_rate above -- observed 2026-09-11, not yet chosen deliberately.
host._spec_audio_io_note: 2 audio in, 2 audio out. Stereo line in; differential line out plus a headphone out.
host.guitar_input_label: left (ch0) -- CONFIRMED 2026-09-13 by direct measurement: bela/io-check-input/ showed the mezzoforte-strummed guitar signal on ch0 (peak -8.8 to -11.6 dBFS across strums) while ch1 stayed at the noise floor (~-64 dBFS, no crosstalk). Matches the mono-guitar-into-stereo-input expectation.
host.exciter_output_label: right (ch1) -- AS WIRED, per Abel 2026-09-13 (Bela out ch1 -> DTA120 right channel -> mono exciter on the guitar body), not yet independently confirmed by the tone-sweep method this note used to suggest. Do that sweep before trusting it for anything safety-relevant.
host._channel_index_note: Guitar input channel confirmed above by direct measurement 2026-09-13. Exciter output channel is per Abel's stated wiring, not yet cross-checked by sending a tone to ch1 and watching it come back on ch0 through the real loop -- still worth doing once real-loop testing starts, since it proves the whole physical chain in one shot.
host._input_buffer_note: Moot for now -- the M4's buffered instrument input sits in front of the Gem's own input regardless (ground-rules 4.1), so this rule is satisfied by construction. Still unmeasured what the Gem's own input would need on its own.

input_signal_check.source: pink noise into the Epiphone's position (guitar -> M4 direct out -> Bela in)
input_signal_check._first_pass_note: Clipping on both channels at default board gain -- source too hot. Abel turned it down.
input_signal_check._second_pass_note: Clean, matched L/R, no clipping. Confirms input signal path end to end. Measured with bela/io-check-input/ (output-silent diagnostic, never writes audioWrite -- cannot drive the exciter). Not the deliberate Phase 1 gain-staging measurement (gain_staging.pickup_into_board_peak_dbfs below is still null).

host._latency_note: MEASURED 2026-09-13 via bela/latency-check/ + host/rig/analyse_latency.py -- Abel's suggestion: a short, quiet (0.08 linear) 1kHz burst emitted on the exciter output channel, arrival found on the pickup channel by normalised cross-correlation. This is the WHOLE round trip -- Bela DAC -> DTA120 (at 100%) -> exciter -> body -> strings -> pickup -> Bela ADC, mechanical/acoustic leg included, not just Bela's own electrical latency. 5 bursts: two tight clusters, 2.15-2.20 ms (3 bursts) and 4.17 ms exactly (2 bursts), median 2.20 ms, spread 2.02 ms. The two clusters are suspiciously exact (184 vs ~96-97 samples both times) -- plausibly a real secondary path/mode rather than noise, not investigated further. First search used a 0.3s window and got 2 wild outliers (58ms, 99ms) from the guitar body's resonant ringing after the burst matching the correlation template almost as well as the real arrival -- narrowed to 0.05s and all 5 became consistent. Sets the phase-condition comb spacing (ground-rules 7/11): at ~2.2ms round trip, comb teeth are roughly 1/0.0022 ≈ 450 Hz apart, i.e. fairly sparse in the guitar's range.
host._spec_analog_in_note: 8 analog inputs, 16-bit, ~22-24 kHz, DC-coupled. Voltage range TBC. Used for the expression pedal (ground-rules 4.3, 8).
host._spec_analog_out_note: None. analogWrite() is not available on Gem. gen1 never used analog out.
host._spec_connectivity_note: USB-C device port for the IDE and gadget networking; USB-A host for WiFi / BT / Ethernet / MIDI; I2C + Qwiic.
host._spec_ide_note: Browser IDE (TypeScript/Vue). C++, Pure Data, SuperCollider supported.

gain_staging._retired_v2_m4_measurements: RETIRED 2026-09-13 (rig-profile v2 -> v3, see _v3_note above). Everything below in this block through pickup_into_board_peak_dbfs describes the M4-based chain, which no longer exists -- kept for the historical record, not as current values. The M4 was removed after being confirmed as a ground-loop source (ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.4). Gain staging has to be redone from scratch via board_input_gain_setting (Bela's own input PGA, 0-59.5 dB) once the replacement passive DI box arrives -- see the new _ground_loop_finding_2026-09-12 note below for what actually happened, and the new direct-connection note under _signal_chain_note for what's wired now.
gain_staging.split_point: RETIRED (v2): M4 instrument input (buffered) -> M4 headphone out -> Bela Gem audio in
gain_staging._split_point_note: Corrected 2026-09-12: the M4 feeds Bela via its HEADPHONE OUT, not a dedicated line/direct out as earlier notes assumed. That gives two independent M4-side gain stages, not one.
gain_staging.m4_preamp_gain_setting: RETIRED (v2): 10:30-10:45 clock position (Abel's more precise reading than the eyeballed percentage; landed there via 0% -> 25% -> 60% (clipped) -> 35% -> 50% -> ~44% -> nudged down slightly)
gain_staging.m4_headphone_out_level: RETIRED (v2): 50% -- was fixed while staging the preamp (Abel, 2026-09-12); moot now the M4 is out of the chain.
gain_staging._m4_note: Two independent gain stages on the M4 alone, both upstream of Bela: the instrument-input preamp (staged live 2026-09-12 against the -12 dBFS peak target below, see pickup_into_board_peak_dbfs) and the headphone-out level feeding Bela in (fixed at 50%, held constant during preamp staging on purpose -- moving both at once would make the preamp reading meaningless). Topology: guitar -> M4 preamp -> M4 headphone out -> Bela in -> DSP -> Bela out -> Dayton DTA120 -> exciter. RETIRED 2026-09-13 along with the rest of this block -- the M4 is no longer in the signal path (ground loop, see below).
gain_staging._ground_loop_finding_2026-09-12: The noise chased through most of 2026-09-12's session was a ground loop: the M4 and Bela were both referencing ground through the same Mac at once (M4 via USB audio, Bela via its USB-C dev tether) while also linked by an analog cable -- two paths back to one ground. Confirmed methodically: a plain Bela-out-to-Bela-in electrical loopback was clean regardless of code/Watcher/CPU load or the status LED; a program that never reads audio input was clean via both the browser IDE and this project's own CLI deploy path; the M4's own output, monitored directly (M4 never touching Bela), was clean; the M4 through Bela on the plainest possible passthrough (zero instrumentation) was noisy on every downstream device tried (Beyerdynamic headphones, Genelec active monitors, the DTA120+exciter chain alike) -- because the noise was already in the signal at Bela's output jack, before any of those. Fix: M4 moved to its own dedicated wall power, off the Mac's USB entirely (it still works standalone as a preamp/buffer this way). That killed the loud/clicky noise; a much quieter 50 Hz hum remained (M4's own supply vs. Bela's Mac-referenced ground, still tied by an unbalanced cable -- ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.4 already anticipated exactly this residual case). Full narrative in ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.4; this note is the pointer.
gain_staging.board_input_gain_setting: 10 dB (Bela's own input PGA, set via build_project.sh's -c '-I -1,10' / the --audio-input-gain flag), CURRENT v3 SETTING, staged live 2026-09-13
gain_staging._v3_gain_staging_note: Redone from scratch 2026-09-13 now that the M4 (and its preamp) is gone -- the only gain stage left is Bela's own onboard PGA (0-59.5 dB range). Iterated live against bela/io-check-input/ while Abel played mezzoforte: 16 dB (board default) showed no signal above the noise floor at all; 50 dB clipped hard (ch0 peak pinned at 0.0 dBFS, RMS -0.3 dBFS -- a near-square wave); 25 dB still clipped (peak pinned at 0.0 dBFS) though less severely (RMS -4 to -6 dBFS); 10 dB landed cleanly on target. Confirms the guitar is very hot even fully unbuffered and unloaded -- removing the M4 didn't just remove a preamp stage, the pickup swings harder without a buffer loading it down at all.
gain_staging.pickup_into_board_peak_dbfs: -8.8 to -11.6 dBFS peak / -19.7 to -23.2 dBFS RMS on ch0, mezzoforte strumming, measured live 2026-09-13 with bela/io-check-input/ at the 10 dB setting above -- right on target, ch1 silent (~-64 dBFS, no crosstalk). RETIRED (v2, M4-chain): -8 to -14 dBFS -- superseded by this measurement, kept above in this block for history only.
gain_staging._target: about -12 dBFS peak on normal playing, so feedback growth has room before clipping
gain_staging._ceiling_note: A safety constant in code. No tuning process may raise it (ground rule 1). It must be reviewed for the Gem's actual output level and sample rate by an EXPLICIT human commit before the first live loop - not silently, not by an optimiser. Code is the authority; this is for the log only.
gain_staging._amp_note: Fixed constant once CHOSEN -- currently mid-measurement, not yet re-fixed, which is different from being a variable under test (ground rule 5 is about not moving it to make a result come out a certain way; deliberately sweeping it IS the Phase 1 measurement ground-rules 11 and the phase plan call for). History: set to 12 o'clock 2026-09-11 (Abel, qualitative -- raw passthrough produced audible feedback when turned up, backed off from there). Held at 12 o'clock through the 2026-09-13 v3 re-measurement, which found zero growth from silence there (see 'loop' below) -- consistent with what Abel heard live moments earlier (increased sustain, no runaway). Abel then deliberately moved it to 100% (max) to bracket the actual unity-gain threshold, per the open question in ground-rules 11 and phase-plan Phase 1 item 5 -- this is that measurement in progress, not a casual change. Once the threshold is bracketed to Abel's satisfaction, the chosen value gets fixed here again and stops moving.

safety.designated_hardware_kill: none required -- DTA120 power switch available as a manual backstop (Abel, 2026-09-11)
safety._kill_note: Deliberate, not missing: Bela audio out feeds the Dayton DTA120 straight into the exciter, no pedal or other device in between. Ground rule (Abel, 2026-09-11): no dedicated hardware kill is required in this build, because there is no second, uncontrolled acoustic loop (nothing feeds a live guitar amp or PA) and the DTA120+exciter's worst case even at full runaway is judged safe. The DTA120's own power switch is a trivial, always-available manual backstop -- not a required interlock, just there. Software kill (output ceiling, mute-on-error, watchdog) stays mandatory regardless. If a hardware kill is ever added back (e.g. a volume pedal), record it here and it becomes required again.
safety._unattended_note: Not granted yet on this rig. Requires Abel to explicitly confirm the rig connected and permit unattended operation, per ground rule 2.

exciter.model: Dayton Audio (surface transducer, exact model TBD)

loop._distrusted_2026-09-12: Abel, end of session: the whole feedback-ramp session below is DISTRUSTED pending hardware verification, not just the retracted 75% take. A clean 'no feedback at all, even at Dayton=100% fully open' result flatly contradicts 2026-09-11's real, heard feedback at Dayton>50% during plain passthrough -- that contradiction is the tell, not a physics finding to build on. Plan: Abel checks cables/connections tomorrow before any of this is trusted or acted on. The ONLY thing from this session still trusted is the M4 preamp gain-staging result (10:30-10:45, see gain_staging above) -- that was validated live, repeatedly, against directly-observed input levels, not inferred from a ramp. Re-run the feedback-ramp measurements fresh once the rig is confirmed sound; don't just re-read these.
loop._distrusted_2026-09-12_update_2026-09-13: The 'hardware check' this note called for happened, and found something bigger than a loose cable: the M4-Bela ground loop documented in gain_staging._ground_loop_finding_2026-09-12 above and ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.4. That ground loop is a very plausible confound for these feedback-ramp readings too (it affects the actual signal at Bela's output, not just what you hear downstream). Combined with the rig physically changing since (v2 -> v3, M4 removed, CLAUDE.md rule 13), these measurements are now retired on two independent grounds, not just distrusted pending a check -- don't resurrect them even if the cable turns out to have been fine. Re-measure fresh under v3 once the DI box is in and gain-staged.
loop._retracted_236.9hz_note: RETRACTED 2026-09-12. The 236.9 Hz seen in logs/2026-09-12/004813_feedback-ramp-signal-75pct.json was NOT the software loop-gain ramp reaching threshold -- Abel confirmed he heard no feedback developing during that take and manually cranked the DTA120 knob to 100% for short periods himself, which is what coincided with that energy. A hardware gain change during a run this project's ramp is supposed to be the only variable in is exactly the kind of confound ground rule 10 (one variable at a time) exists to prevent. The log record's audio/metrics are left untouched as an honest record of what was actually captured (confound included); this note is the correction to how it was being interpreted. Do not treat 236.9 Hz as a real candidate.
loop._ramp_measurements_2026-09-12: DISTRUSTED, see the note above -- kept for reference, not as findings. Via bela/feedback-ramp/ (software loop-gain ramped 0->1 over 60s at a fixed DTA120/M4 setting, held at 1 after, watchdog auto-mutes at 120s -- the one part of this that DID check out, confirmed firing correctly on real hardware both times a run went to completion). DTA120=50%, silence -- flat -80 to -85 dBFS through a full 50s hold at loop-gain=1, no growth (logs/2026-09-12/004402_feedback-ramp-silence.json). DTA120=75%, Abel playing + confounded by a manual mid-run DTA120 change -- retracted separately, see above. DTA120=100% (maximum), silence, clean/unconfounded on its own terms -- flat -78 to -80 dBFS through the full 60s hold at loop-gain=1, no growth (logs/2026-09-12/005304_feedback-ramp-silence-100pct.json). This no-growth-at-all-even-at-max result is exactly what triggered the distrust above: it contradicts real heard feedback on 2026-09-11 at Dayton>50%. Something in the chain -- a cable, a connection, which channel is actually recorded, anything -- is suspect, not the physics.
loop._note: First feedback heard on this platform 2026-09-11, during the bela/gen1-passthrough/ smoke test, with the DTA120 turned up above its 12-o'clock setting -- not measured or recorded (no frequency, no gain value), just confirmed audible by Abel. This is the reference the 2026-09-12 ramp results contradict and were distrusted against, not something the ramp results get to overrule. unity_gain_master_setting and transfer_function_measurement remain null pending a verified rig and a clean re-measurement.
loop._v3_ramp_2026-09-13_dta120_12oclock_sile: Clean re-measurement, ground-loop-free, channel-routing-bug-free (see bela/gen1-passthrough and bela/feedback-ramp 2026-09-13 header notes -- both output channels now duplicate the mono guitar input, previously out ch1 silently read the guitar's unused/silent ch1). At DTA120=12 o'clock (the provisional setting from gain_staging), full 150s run (60s ramp 0->1, 60s hold at 1, 120s watchdog): zero sustained growth anywhere, analysed offline with host/rig/analyse_take.py (sustained_fraction=0.00, onset=never). NOT contradicted this time -- corroborated by Abel directly hearing/feeling only increased sustain, no runaway, moments earlier on bela/gen1-passthrough at the same DTA120 setting. Consistent physics: a sub-unity loop assists a played note but has nothing to grow from silence alone.
loop._v3_ramp_2026-09-13_dta120_100pct_silenc: DTA120 turned to 100% (max) for this run, same 10 dB input gain from gain_staging. Watched live via a script polling in_peak/out_peak/loop_gain/muted at 20 Hz (host-side, not committed -- see this session's transcript) and stopped the board the instant sustained growth crossed -20 dBFS, rather than letting the full ramp run blind. Result: loop_gain sat at exactly 1.000 (ramp fully complete) for roughly 20s with output flat at the -33 to -38 dBFS noise floor, then grew -- clearly exponential, tracking in/out together, not a digital artefact -- from about -30 dBFS to -18.4 dBFS over the next ~11s before the script stopped it. Growth rate near threshold is gentle (~1 dB/s average, accelerating), consistent with the loop sitting just above unity rather than deeply over it. Reading: at DTA120=100%, the acoustic loop only crosses unity once software loop-gain is itself very close to 1.0 -- the amp alone, even fully open, doesn't put the loop far above threshold. unity_gain_master_setting below is a first bound from this, not a final answer -- Abel's plan is to narrow it further (intermediate DTA120 settings) next.
loop.unity_gain_master_setting_note: First bound, 2026-09-13: at DTA120=100% (max), threshold requires loop_gain approx 1.0 (see note above). At DTA120=12 o'clock, loop_gain=1.0 for a full 60s hold produced no growth at all -- threshold is above 1.0 there, i.e. unreachable by this software ramp alone (which caps at 1.0). The real unity crossing as a function of DTA120 position is therefore somewhere between 12 o'clock and 100% -- not yet bracketed further than that.

control._control_note: An analog input (the Gem has 8) - a passive expression pedal per ground-rules 4.3, calibrated from analog_in_voltage_range once measured. MIDI over the USB-A host is available as a fallback.

baseline._note: The 'before' recordings: the loop feeding back with no regulation, at several master-gain positions. None recorded on this platform yet.
